faqs.question: My printouts are dark when I print from Photoshop CS3 or later. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
While we do not assist with color profiling or color correction, you can try the                 following:
Use latest version of Adobe Photoshop.
Make sure your print head nozzles are clean and free from clogs.
Make the following adjustment in Adobe Photoshop:
Select
Color Management
or
Output
>
Output
from Photoshop's print                             screen.
Click
Transfer
and drag the middle of the curve                             to 40.0%.
Click
OK
, then select
Color                                 Management
.
Select
Let Photoshop manage color as normal
and                             the appropriate printer profile.
Print your image. Because every photo is different, you may need to                             experiment with the Transfer Curve to find the level that best suits                             your needs.
Note:
Making changes to the Transfer Curve does not alter                                 the original image. This curve affects the Shadows, Midtones, and                                 Highlights as a whole.
Make the following adjustments in the Windows or Mac driver to lighten the                         image:
Adjust the Gamma setting to 1.8.
Increase the Brightness bar to 5.
Note:
If using a Mac, make sure the                                 Color Mode is EPSON Standard sRGB.
See the product's User Guide for more information in these settings.

faqs.question: There are vertical bands or lines on my printout.  What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Run three auto print head alignments.
Make sure High Speed is not selected.
Lower the dpi setting you selected to print.  If you selected 2880 dpi, lower                     the setting to 1440 dpi.
Make sure the lines are not in the image source.
Make sure you use the correct profile settings.

Epson Presentation Paper Matte

HEAD ALIGNMENT

Make sure
Auto

faqs.question: I am having trouble manually loading media into the rear manual feed slot. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Make sure that the product is turned on and READY appears on the LCD.
Attach the rear sheet guide to the back of the product.
Slide the left edge guide to the left so it is slightly wider than the width of                     your paper.
Insert one sheet face up and short edge first into the rear sheet guide against                     the right edge guide.
Slide the left edge guide against the left edge of the paper.
Gently guide the paper into the slot until it meets resistance.  Maintain a                     constant pressure; after a few seconds you'll feel the product pull the paper                     into printing position.
Use both hands to pull out and extend the output tray, lifting it slightly as                     you pull. Make sure the arrow marks on the tray and the printer are aligned.

faqs.question: I can't find the Fine Art paper option in Windows. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Load the media in the printer, then select the paper path (
Manual - Rear
or
Manual - Front
) as your paper source in the printer driver. You see the Fine Art media choices. See your product's User's Guide to determine which black ink to use for your media type.

faqs.question: My ICC profiles do not appear in Mac OS X 10.1 to 10.6. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The operating system may prevent the ICC profiles from installing correctly. Do the following             to copy the ICC profiles to the correct location:
Note:
Close all image editing software                 before you begin.
Open the hard drive and select
Library
>
Printers
>
EPSON
>
InkjetPrinters
>
ICCProfiles
folders.
Hold down the control key on your                     keyboard and then click on the file with the .profiles suffix.
From the new window, select
Show Package Contents
.
Next, select the
Contents
then the
Resources
folder.
Copy all ICC profiles in the Resources                     folder.
Open the hard drive and select
Library
>
Colorsync
>
Profiles
folders and then paste the copied ICC profiles.
